subject: Private deployment: BYOK custody, operator access, and cross-border safeguards
messages:
From: Maya R. <maya.sec@solsticehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@solsticehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy — BYOK custody, operator access & cross-border safeguards

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking a look at our private deployment questions. We're evaluating Redwood for a VPC-hosted/private deployment in two phases: (1) US production inside our AWS account, (2) a small on-prem PoC in our EU facility later this year. Before we proceed we need clarity on three items that our legal/security teams flagged in the DPA review:

1) Keystore custody model and escrow: we need a clear statement of whether Redwood will ever have access to plaintext customer keys for BYOK deployments, and how keystore escrow/escrow retrieval is handled (procedural steps + audit samples).
2) Operator/service-account access: what specific operator roles (if any) require key access for breakglass or maintenance? We need an operator access matrix and justification for each role.
3) Cross-border routing & data flow: if the control plane is in the US but inference runtime is in EU on-prem, what telemetry/metadata is transferred and which elements are encrypted with customer keys vs Redwood keys?

Practical asks: can you share an example operator access matrix and a sanitized evidence sample showing limited operator access during a maintenance window? Also any language we can reuse for our DPA (narrower subprocessor scope, jurisdiction commitments) would help speed procurement.

Appreciate a concise reply we can forward to our InfoSec team.

—Maya
Security Lead, Solstice Health
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya R. <maya.sec@solsticehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy — BYOK custody, operator access & cross-border safeguards

Maya — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by attachments and a proposed operational playbook.

1) Keystore custody/escrow: Redwood does NOT hold plaintext customer keys for BYOK. For private/VPC and on-prem BYOK, customers provision and control a customer-managed key (CMK) in their KMS or on-prem HSM. We offer an optional keystore-escrow protocol only when requested for business continuity; escrow is encrypted under a secondary escrow KEK that is held by a third-party escrow agent and released only under documented legal and operational triggers (see evidence sample).

2) Operator access: our standard private-deploy operator model is "no-plaintext, least-privilege." Operator roles are limited to orchestration and network support; only a named breakglass procedurally-approved SRE can request temporary access and must provide an audit ticket. We do not, as policy, perform key import/export in plaintext. Attached: operator access matrix (redacted) and a sanitized evidence sample from a prior maintenance window.

3) Cross-border telemetry: control plane signals (job IDs, error counters, anonymized runtime metrics) may route to Redwood control plane in the US for orchestration. Any customer data (inputs, outputs, model state) stored in the runtime is encrypted at rest and in transit; when BYOK is used those payloads are encrypted under the customer's CMK such that Redwood cannot decrypt. We can provide a control-plane-only deployment option (control plane in-customer-VPC / private control-plane) for EU data residency.

Attachments: privdep-operator-access-matrix.xlsx, evidence-sample-keystore-audit.pdf

Next steps: Dev and Karthik — can you confirm the minimal operator entitlements we need to include in the DPA addendum and draft a suggested clause for escrow triggers (court order / joint incident response / customer request)? Maya — if you want a control-plane-only option we can scope that separately; it affects SLA and upgrade window.

Best,
Evelyn
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Maya R. <maya.sec@solsticehealth.com>

Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy — BYOK custody, operator access & cross-border safeguards

On Wed, Jul 15, 2025 at 11:03 AM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Maya — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by attachments and a proposed operational playbook.

Thanks — adding technical detail here.

Operator entitlements (summary):
- SRE-Orchestrator: can restart services, apply infra configs, view anonymized runtime logs. No access to CMK ciphertext keys or plaintext.
- SRE-Network: can access VPC/SG configs, no keystore permissions.
- Breakglass-SRE: for emergencies only, issues require a JIRA ticket ID + approval from 2 on-call leads and CTO designee; access is time-limited and session-recorded.

Escrow flow (high level):
- Customer elects escrow at onboarding; escrow KEK generated by third-party (e.g., Entrust) and wrapped by customer CMK.
- Escrow retrieval requires signed retrieval request, two legal approvals from Redwood, and a notarized release from the escrow agent.

Telemetry & metadata specifics:
- Control plane: job metadata (job_id, route, worker-region), aggregated latency stats, and anonymized failure codes.
- No customer PII or prompt text is sent to Redwood control plane when BYOK + private runtime is used, unless customer enables telemetry opt-in for support.

Attached is a one-page recommended DPA paragraph and a redlined escrow trigger clause for your counsel to review.

—Dev
Director, Private Deploy Engineering

Evelyn / Dev — this is exactly what we needed, thank you. Jared and I will pass the operator matrix and the escrow clause to procurement and our counsel. Two quick clarifications:

1) For the EU PoC, can we get the control-plane-only option costs and an estimated lead time?
2) For the evidence sample: can you confirm the redaction removes any customer identifiers and that session recordings are retained for 90 days (our audit ask)?

If both answers are positive we'll proceed to a short SOW and request the DPA addendum redline.

Thanks again — Maya
Security Lead, Solstice Health
